references.text: The preceding verses in the same passage deal with the eye as the body's lamp and warn that the light within you must not be darkness. [ref:Luk 11:34-35|Luke 11:34-35] forms the immediate context for the promise in verse 36 that the whole body should be full of light.

Jesus' parallel teaching in the Sermon on the Mount about the eye as the body's lamp: [ref:Matt 6:22-23|Matthew 6:22-23]. The same image of the bright versus the dark eye is used to illustrate spiritual receptivity.

In [ref:Matt 5:14-16|Matthew 5:14-16], Jesus speaks about disciples being the light of the world and that their light should shine before others—a thematic parallel to the whole body being enlightened and functioning as light.

Paul writes in [ref:Ef 5:8-9|Ephesians 5:8-9] that believers once were darkness, but now are light in the Lord, and urges them to walk as children of light. This is a thematic parallel to the whole body being full of light.

In [ref:1 Tess 5:5|1 Thessalonians 5:5], believers are called "children of light and children of the day", which reflects the promise in Luke 11:36 about being fully enlightened, without any darkness.
Peter compares the prophetic word to a lamp (λύχνος) shining in a dark place in [ref:2 Pet 1:19|2 Peter 1:19]. The lamp motif is the same as in Luke 11:36, where the lamp shines with its radiance.

[ref:Sal 119:105|Psalm 119:105] says that God's word is a lamp for our feet and a light for our path. The image of a lamp giving light runs throughout Scripture, paralleling the lamp that shines in Luke 11:36.

[ref:Ordsp 20:27|Proverbs 20:27] says that the human spirit is the Lord's lamp, searching all the innermost parts of the body. This reflects the image of the whole person being enlightened from within, as described in Luke 11:36.

In [ref:Jes 60:1-2|Isaiah 60:1-2], the people are called to arise and shine, for their light has come and the glory of the Lord shines upon them. The contrast between light and darkness and being fully enlightened is thematically linked to Luke 11:36.

[ref:Luk 11:33|Luke 11:33] introduces the entire passage with the image of a lamp placed on a stand to give light, forming the basis for the conclusion in verse 36 that the whole body should be full of light when the lamp shines upon you with its radiance.
